tldr: This thread is grouped by a shared "Same X, Different Y" title pattern, not by one event; what links the items is variance in agent and eval results that does not come from the model. It opened Nov 1-3 with a 17-point gap between agents on one model, an IBM harness comparison, and an arXiv audit of multimodal benchmark graders.
whats_new: A Nov 19 arXiv paper reports that the design of the numerical scoring scheme affects how reliable LLM-as-a-Judge evaluation is, extending the earlier grader audit from benchmark parsers to judge models.
why_it_matters: Harness, error delivery and scoring scheme each move agent scores with the model held fixed, so a model-only comparison can misattribute a gain or regression.

beats.headline: Same model, different harness: a 17-point gap and IBM's CUGA comparison
beats.summary: A blog post and an IBM Research post compare agent harnesses wrapped around one model.

beats.headline: Multimodal benchmark scoring rules change scores on identical outputs
beats.summary: An arXiv audit of the unjustified code that turns free-form answers into right/wrong verdicts.

beats.headline: Error delivery and multi-agent testbeds probe agent behavior
beats.summary: One paper studies how the placement of tool-error feedback changes retry, fix or stop decisions; another releases a supply-chain arena for four LLM agents.

beats.headline: LLM-as-a-Judge scores depend on the numerical scoring scheme
beats.summary: An arXiv paper on how scoring-scheme design affects judge reliability.

open_questions: Does the MCP post publish its harness differences, prompts and scoring method so the 17-point gap can be reproduced?
Does the IBM CUGA post report numbers on a shared benchmark, and can they be rerun?
Which scoring scale does the LLM-as-a-Judge paper find most stable, and by how much does agreement change?
Does the error-delivery paper give a recommended place to return tool errors that harness authors can adopt?
take_for_builders: Hold the model fixed and vary the harness, tool-error format and judge scoring scale in your own eval before attributing a score change to the model; treat the 17-point and CUGA figures as blog or vendor results until reproduced.
